question: Evaluate $\int \sin^3 x\cos^2 x\,dx$ by transforming the integrand suitably and using an appropriate substitution.
explanation:
To apply substitution effectively, separate one factor of $\sin x$ and express the remaining even power of sine in terms of cosine. Using $\sin^2 x=1-\cos^2 x$,

$$\int \sin^3 x\cos^2 x\,dx=\int \sin x\left(1-\cos^2 x\right)\cos^2 x\,dx$$

Expanding the integrand,

$$\int \sin^3 x\cos^2 x\,dx=\int \sin x\left(\cos^2 x-\cos^4 x\right)dx$$

Put $t=\cos x$. Then $dt=-\sin x\,dx$, so $\sin x\,dx=-dt$. Therefore,

$$\int \sin^3 x\cos^2 x\,dx=-\int \left(t^2-t^4\right)dt$$

$$=-\int t^2dt+\int t^4dt$$

Integrating term by term,

$$=-\frac{t^3}{3}+\frac{t^5}{5}+C$$

Substituting $t=\cos x$ back,

$$\int \sin^3 x\cos^2 x\,dx=-\frac{\cos^3 x}{3}+\frac{\cos^5 x}{5}+C$$

Hence, the required integral is $\frac{\cos^5 x}{5}-\frac{\cos^3 x}{3}+C$.
